terms.x: a handle to a running thread
terms.p: The value thread::spawn gives back, whose join method waits for that thread to finish and hands you what it returned.

terms.x: traits the compiler implements for you
terms.p: Traits like Send and Sync that nobody writes an impl for: the compiler decides a type has them if every one of its fields does.

terms.x: proof that you hold the lock
terms.p: The value a lock call returns, which gives access to the data inside the mutex and releases the lock when it is dropped.
The flag a mutex sets when a thread panics while holding it, so later lockers are told the data may have been left half-updated.

terms.x: two threads waiting on each other
terms.p: Two or more threads each holding a lock the other needs, so none of them can ever continue.

terms.x: a thread that cannot outlive its scope
terms.p: A thread started inside thread::scope, which the compiler knows will be joined before the scope ends, so it may borrow local variables.
An operation the hardware guarantees no other core can observe halfway through, which is how a counter can be shared without a lock.

terms.x: a full queue slowing the producer
terms.p: What a bounded channel gives you: once it is full the sender blocks, so a fast producer cannot pile up unbounded work for a slow consumer.
